Before writing any code, present the user with the structure of the stack that you intend to submit and ask for confirmation before proceeding.\\n\\nDO NOT use `git commit` or `git push`. Instead, you must use the following Graphite commands:\\n  Instead of `git commit`, use `gt create`. This will create a commit and a branch with the current changes.\\n  Instead of `git push`, use `gt submit --no-interactive`. This will submit the current branch & all downstack branches to Graphite.\\n\\nOnce you've received confirmation to build a stack, follow these steps carefully:\\n\\n1. Write the code for the first pull request. YOU MUST ALWAYS write the code BEFORE creating the branch. This allows the user to validate if they are happy with the changes before they are committed.\\n\\n2. Stage the changes with `git add`.\\n\\n3. Create the first branch with `gt create`.\\n  - Follow any previous instructions about crafting commit messages, and provide the message as a parameter to `gt create` using the `--message` flag.\\n  - Keep in mind that the first line of the commit message will become the title of the PR.\\n\\n4. Repeat steps 1-3 for each subsequent pull request in the stack.\\n\\n5. When you've finished writing the code for the last pull request, submit the stack with `gt submit --no-interactive`.\\n  - After submission, present the user with the /github/pr/ link to the first PR in the stack.\\n\\n\\nUSAGE\\n  $ gt <command> [flags]\\n\\nTERMS\\n  stack:     A sequence of pull requests, each building off of its parent. (ex: main <- PR \\\"add API\\\" <- PR \\\"update frontend\\\" <- PR \\\"docs\\\")\\n  trunk:     The branch that stacks are merged into. (ex: main)\\n  downstack: The PRs below the given PR in a stack, i.e. its ancestors.\\n  upstack:   The PRs above the given PR in a stack, i.e. its descendants.\\n\\nCORE COMMANDS\\n  gt init: Initializes your Git repo to work with Graphite\\n  gt create: Creates a new branch and commit your changes\\n  gt submit: Submits the current branch & all downstack branches to Graphite\\n  gt submit --stack: Submits your current stack to Graphite\\n  gt modify: Amends your current branch with new changes and rebases all PRs above it\\n  gt restack: Rebases every PR in a stack to have the latest changes\\n  gt sync: Pulls the latest trunk branch, rebases all open PRs/stacks on top of the latest changes, and prompts to delete any stale/old/merged branches\\n  gt checkout: Interactively checks out any of your branches\\n  gt state: Prints out the state of the repository\\n  gt up: Checks out the branch directly upstack\\n  gt down: Checks out the branch directly downstack\\n\\nCORE WORKFLOW\\n  Run the learn tool to learn how to use gt.\\n\\nTo run a `gt` command, call this tool.\"}"}
